news.title: Trump links under fresh spotlight as FIFA flags unthinkable sale
news.lede: FIFA’s plans to sell a minority stake that has the potential to reshape the World Cup, the jewel in football’s crown, has been flamed by experts, with president Gianni Infantino in line to profit from the scheme. FIFA announced its plans to create a new commercial subsidiary on Wednesday (AEST) that will operate its main events, like the World Cup, in a move that Infantino claims could triple the amount of money for member associations. news.title: FIFA boss Infantino unveils $20b plan to sell World Cup to Kushner consortium
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino (left) has plans to sell the World Cup to a consortium that includes Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared. (Getty Images: Chris Brunskill). FIFA president Gianni Infantino is planning to create a $US20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors. One of the intended investors is Thrive Eternal, a company launched by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is a son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

news.title: Burnham blasts FIFA plan to sell World Cup commercial rights
news.lede: “The World Cup is not a product,” said Britain’s prime minister. “Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hit out at plans announced by FIFA to sell a chunk of commercial rights linked to the football World Cup. Under the plan, which has provoked a furious reaction from European football association governing body UEFA, FIFA would create an investment vehicle holding commercial rights related to the World Cup and sell a portion of it to investors for $4.2 billion.

news.title: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino attends a World Cup match between Netherlands and Morocco at Monterrey Stadium, in Guadalupe, Mexico, on June 29, 2026. Carl Recine/Getty Images South America hide caption. Just days after staging the most lucrative World Cup in history, FIFA has a new — and instantly controversial — plan to raise more money: selling stakes in its marquee event to private investors for billions of dollars. It's a complicated but potentially lucrative plan, one that comes as FIFA is still facing strong criticism for jacking up ticket prices for the 2026 World Cup across North America.

news.title: ‘Not yours to sell’: WC plunged into turmoil as FIFA ‘nuclear bomb’ set to spark stunning revolt
news.lede: FIFA said Tuesday it plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions through the creation of a semi-private subsidiary. World football’s governing body said it would retain a majority share in FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) but hoped to raise $4.2 billion later this year by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests”. news.title: FIFA wants to sell World Cup stake to private investors: UEFA isn't happy and here's why
news.lede: FIFA announced a controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors on Tuesday, one that UEFA quickly slammed as a "line that football's governing institutions should never cross." FIFA boss Gianni Infantino unveiled the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a new organization that would oversee commercial rights and operational delivery via a $20 billion company with private investors including the Kushner family. UEFA, the European governing body of soccer, immediately reacted on the news saying it "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross." The proposal is subject to approval by a majority of those national associations and FIFA's 37-member council.
